raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Under prefill context parallelism, each QSA layer runs two all-gathers: one for the index keys and one for the layer's K/V. The following changes reduce synchronization overhead and overlap communication with computation. ### 1. Remove Host–Device Synchronizations The first change removes four host–device synchronizations per layer on this path, or five when using a cached prefix: - The `positions.max().item()` call in the indexer's RoPE. - The `.tolist()` conversion of sequence lengths. - The prefix's request-index `.tolist()` conversion, when using a cached prefix. - The per-layer `torch.tensor` copy that builds the sparse-attention kernel's K offsets. - The sparse-attention kernel's `max_q.item()` call. Three of these synchronizations, or four with a cached prefix, occurred immediately after an all-gather. As a result, every rank's CPU waited for the slowest rank on each layer, and the GPU then sat idle while the CPU relaunched work. Removing these synchronizations lets the CPU run ahead. This saves: - CP4: approximately 8 ms at both 8K and 32K, reducing latency by 27.5% and 11.7%, respectively. - CP8: approximately 3–8.5 ms at 8K and 32K, reducing latency by 12.1% and 19.4%, respectively. There is no numeric change. ### 2. Overlap the K/V All-Gather with the Indexer The second change overlaps the K/V all-gather with the indexer. A hook fires immediately after the indexer issues its own key gather and starts the K/V gather on a side stream. The K/V gather then runs during: - Compression. - MQA scoring. - Top-k selection. Attention waits for the gather only when it needs the result. The index-key gather stays inline: it is short, and its long waits come from load imbalance, which overlap cannot hide. This provides additional latency reductions: - At 32K: 1.5 ms on CP4 and 1.85 ms on CP8, or 2.5% and 5.3%, respectively. - At 128K: approximately 7 ms. - At the 8K first chunk: neutral overall, because the layer is limited by kernel launch speed. ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling CP4 | Shape | Main | Commit 1 | Commit 1 gain | Commit 2 | Commit 2 gain (over Commit 1) | Total gain | |-------|-----:|---------:|--------------:|---------:|-----------------------------:|-----------:| | 8K | 29.24 | 21.19 | −8.05 (−27.5%) | 21.49 | +0.30 (+1.4%)¹ | −7.75 (−26.5%) | | 32K | 68.45 | 60.44 | −8.02 (−11.7%) | 58.94 | −1.50 (−2.5%) | −9.52 (−13.9%) | | 128K | 431.42 | 425.53 | −5.89 (−1.4%) | 418.46 | −7.07 (−1.7%) | −12.96 (−3.0%) | CP8 | Shape | Main | Commit 1 | Commit 1 gain | Commit 2 | Commit 2 gain (over Commit 1) | Total gain | |-------|-----:|---------:|--------------:|---------:|-----------------------------:|-----------:| | 8K | 24.52 | 21.56 | −2.96 (−12.1%) | 21.25 | −0.31 (−1.4%) | −3.27 (−13.3%) | | 32K | 43.57 | 35.11 | −8.46 (−19.4%) | 33.26 | −1.85 (−5.3%) | −10.32 (−23.7%) | | 128K | 229.28 | 222.51 | −6.77 (−3.0%) | 215.77 | −6.74 (−3.0%) | −13.51 (−5.9%) | This is the nsys timeline before this PR. There are two areas that we should pay attention. In the first area, we have some device and host sync overhead. In the second area, the kv cache allgather is serial function call. After we merge this PR, the kv cache allgather for new generated kv can be issued earlier and overlap with indexer computation. However, the allgather takes longer time because we do not use the 0SM comm. This will be integrated after the 0SM #44029 merged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39539850826](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39539850826) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39539850792](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39539850792) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39539850831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39539850831)
